correctness.rationale: For the full cycloid, the exact two-angle chord identity bounds every distance by 2(d+sin d)≤2πr, with unique equality at the cusp endpoints. Taylor expansion gives the uniform two-cusp deficit a_Lt³+a_Rs³+O(t⁴+s⁴) and each arclength density 2|b_i|t dt. Change of variables to cubic deficits proves the explicit coefficient via Γ(2/3)²/Γ(7/3) and the conditional Dirichlet(2/3,2/3,1) law. Intrinsic normalization uses the verified cusp-curvature determinant definition. Direct quadrature at three deficits, a marked-moment check and 20,100 grid comparisons were replayed from check.py as diagnostics; they are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A cycloid is an archetypal singular planar curve, and its intrinsic 3/2-cuspidal curvature was already mathematically motivated in differential geometry. The new sharp 4/3 extreme-chord exponent and exact constant expose a different rare geometry from smooth ovals, with a complete joint limit law and a scalar inverse relation between an observed tail and the two cusp curvatures. The general result is a reproducible boundary principle for nondegenerate diametral cusps, not a chosen arbitrary numerical parameter slice; precise scope and unproved extensions are explicit.
